parsed.reason: The plan is strongly grounded in the playbook. It names the method (iron-first solids with early-and-often allergens), gives one line of why (iron stores running low, LEAP ~80% reduction), and mentions baby-led weaning in a clause. Readiness signs, Day 1, Days 2-7, week 2 peanut with the 10-minute wait and 2-hour watch, then one allergen every day or two, twice-weekly maintenance, 9-month lumpy textures, and the stop-and-see-provider trigger all match the playbook. It uses no US big-9 framing, no invented spacing, and no dose, medicine or phone number. Tone is warm and non-lecturing. Weaknesses: the 'expect' section is thin. It says gagging is noisy and normal but does not say refusal is normal or that it may look like failing, and it gives no explicit 'how to tell it's working' cue. It also omits the 911 anaphylaxis signs, which is a notable safety gap for an allergy question. 'Peanut allergy cut by roughly 80%' lacks the 'in high-risk infants' qualifier. The check-in day (Friday) is present. Overall it is a solid, actionable plan with gaps in expectations and safety escalation.
